The **Enterprise segment (Enterprise Plan)** offers the strongest growth quality among the three customer segments. It shows the highest satisfaction (NPS 52) [NL-012-S03] [NL-011-S08] [NL-016-S03], the lowest monthly logo churn (1.3%) [NL-012-S03] [NL-016-S03], and the highest expansion revenue in Q2 ($91,000, representing 52.6% of all expansion revenue) [NL-012-S05] [NL-012-S03]. Enterprise also has the best LTV:CAC ratio (16.0x versus 8.3x for SMB) [NL-016-S03], and it is the most valuable segment with an average ACV of $112,000 [NL-011-S08].

Despite this strong growth quality, the Enterprise segment still requires significantly more implementation capacity because it has the longest onboarding duration (average 8.7 weeks) due to permission-mapping challenges and security reviews [NL-012-S03] [NL-015-S03]. These accounts prioritize audit compliance, security, logical database isolation, and require detailed compliance reviews, custom DPAs, and permanent audit log retention windows, which add complexity to the implementation phase [NL-011-S08]. Additionally, the median enterprise onboarding duration of 8.7 weeks is a resource constraint that requires automated tools to streamline permission mapping and improve the initial document cleanup process [NL-012-S09]. Their sentiment is also vulnerable to delays during the implementation phase, necessitating dedicated CSM support and careful resource allocation [NL-011-S08].
